verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents creating and managing its own API Access Tokens, which authenticate users and grant access to resources such as CKS clusters and VPCs. Group-based access control appears only in AI Object Storage bucket policies, and quotas are an adjacent capacity control rather than spend governance. Missing for 10: documented team-member management with roles/RBAC, per-token scoping or permission limits, spend or budget controls tied to users or keys, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can manage team members with roles and scoped API keys so credentials and spend stay controlled

citations.quote: API Access Tokens authenticate users and grant access to resources such as CKS clusters and VPCs.
This page explains how to create, use, and manage API Access Tokens and the kubeconfig files generated alongside them, so you can authenticate kubectl to CKS clusters and keep credentials secure.
CoreWeave AI Object Storage bucket policies now support group-based access control, letting you grant or restrict access based on a principal's group memberships rather than listing individual users.
